title: cli: Fix copying global profile to personal at startup
description:
Fix up commit 1eeb0c99345701dd5698a5a36ff8f87857422b02
At initial startup, the hash of configuration files used
by profiles doesn't exist yet. (Files are only added to
the list after initially parsing the current configuration.)

So, if copying a global profile to the personal directory
at initial startup, just copy all the files from the global
profile.

notes.body: I don't like the "Just copy all the files" part, the list of files which belongs in a profile is made for a reason and I have put a lot of work into making this work.
When thinking about this again it's maybe not an issue when copying from a global profile, because this should not have any other files present.

I can put an extra check in so that this only happens when copying from a global profile.

It's not ideal; the issue is that `profile_files` is only populated at the same time that preferences are initially read from each file (with a tiny difference in the behavior of `io_graphs` and `import_hexdump.json` which aren't read at startup, only registered, but are also registered after other preferences are read.)

For this purpose, it would probably be better to separately populate `profile_files` before reading the switch profile configuration option and doing initial configuration from the profile.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8686/diffs?diff_id=519156634&start_sha=9ab9f0f26f4295b72ad2eb16320d40e1c22ac8f4#3a9191283cda933433cbff7b074876dd674f96b6_1785_1785)
I didn't catch the commit 1eeb0c99345701dd5698a5a36ff8f87857422b02 before now, but you should not duplicate code which should be made as a filesystem.c function.
Can you try making this block of copy "from_file" "to_file" common? They are almost identical, and having an extra `file_exists()` in the block above does not hurt.

Sure. The `test_for_directory(filename)` already does a `stat`, so while it doesn't really hurt to have an extra one, possibly doing one call and looking at the return value would be slightly more efficient. (Check the `test_for_directory()` return against 0, or against EISDIR and ENOENT.)

I'm also tempted to change the call from `g_hash_table_get_keys` to using GHashTableIter, since `g_hash_table_get_keys` iterates over the hash table to generate the list, which is then iterated a second time. Doing that might make it easier to make the block of code common.

It would be slightly easier to combine the code by switching from iterating over `profile_files` in the standard case to iterating over the list of files in the from directory either way, and just check to see if each files is in `profile_files` before copying.

That's slightly less efficient in the case of the from directory having a lot of files not in profile_files, but it saves on trying to `stat` possible configuration files that don't exist.
Note that a profile directory is not supposed to have other files (except from the default which will have non-profile files), so efficiency should not be a big issue.

@stigbjorlykke, any objections currently? I would like to be able to copy a global profile to personal at initial startup from the command line and I don't see another obvious way.
Can we make this explicit with a new parameter `bool copy_all_files` to clearly indicate that all files should be copied, not just the ones which belongs in a profile?
Or maybe even simpler and more consistent to always copy all files when `from_global` is set?

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8686/diffs?diff_id=528870953&start_sha=23f2e58f498364b94f78e5b5049de04ed1ca3eb8#3a9191283cda933433cbff7b074876dd674f96b6_1786_1823)
Do you need to check for `!profile_files` here?
No, because it won't be `NULL` if `do_store_persconffiles` is `TRUE`. Though I probably will change everything to just copy everything if `from_global` is set.

However, even though I don't need to, `do_store_persconffiles` can be `FALSE` when `profile_files` exists, and then with this implementation we wouldn't be using the list of files. One or the other has to be tested (or `from_global`), because `g_hash_table_contains` has a warning if called on a NULL hashtable.

Checking both tests the two cases where the function is called either very early (and `profile_files` is still NULL) or when profile files are still being added to the hashtable (and `do_store_persconffiles` is TRUE). If we assumed that the function would never be called at the wrong time I wouldn't have to do that.

Though if you think it's simpler conceptually to just copy everything whenever it's a global directory, I understand.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8686/diffs?diff_id=528870953&start_sha=23f2e58f498364b94f78e5b5049de04ed1ca3eb8#3a9191283cda933433cbff7b074876dd674f96b6_1785_1823)

The current design is that `profile_files` is populated at startup because we are trying to load every config file (except the UI specific ones). If this should be populated earlier we need to implement a dry-run, which may increase startup time. I think the current solution is ok for now, a global profile is not supposed to have other files.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8686/diffs?diff_id=528870953&start_sha=23f2e58f498364b94f78e5b5049de04ed1ca3eb8#3a9191283cda933433cbff7b074876dd674f96b6_1791_1823)
Can you also make a common "filesystem.c" function for all cases where we copy from a global profile? I think this will increase readability for this specific functionality.

Here it is as a separate function, I think it is more readable.

The case where we are using the list of configuration files is the same logic as originally, though I switched from getting the list of keys to parsing the hashtable once with an iterator, which is mildly more efficient.

I also made a small fix where `to_dir` and `from_dir` were being freed even in the case of errors where the calling functions were using them.
Does this resolve your concerns?

@stigbjorlykke , I think this fixes all your concerns but I didn't want to merge it until you could take a look. The current state of the code without this is a little broken as it will create an empty local profile if a valid global profile name is given on the command line, instead of copying the global profile.
I think my concerns are resolved, this use case is a valid exception to copy all files.

commits_data.message:
cli: Fix copying global profile to personal at startup

Fix up commit 1eeb0c99345701dd5698a5a36ff8f87857422b02
At initial startup, the hash of configuration files used
by profiles doesn't exist yet or is not completely filled.
(Files are only added to the list after initially parsing
the current configuration.)

So, if copying a global profile to the personal directory
at initial startup, just copy all the files from the global
profile.

Also, don't free to_dir and from_dir if we're returning them
in the case of errors.
